headline: South Asia: Israeli strikes kill UNRWA worker, two others in Gaza
script:
Good evening. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Israeli strikes kill UNRWA worker, two others in Gaza.
- India: Russia claims strikes on Starlink terminals, drone sites in Ukraine's Sumy.
- Africa: Ethiopia: Lethal Artillery Strikes On Civilian Neighbourhoods in Tigray's Alamata City Must Be Investigated As War Crimes.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Trump reluctantly orders Army to pause detonation of unstable ammunition.
- Military Times, 9 hours ago: Trump reluctantly orders Army to pause detonation of unstable ammunition.
Trump said he wanted to move forward with the controlled blasts but is putting the decision in the hands of the courts.
- Military Times, 13 hours ago: B-2 bomber wings awarded Presidential Unit Citation for Midnight Hammer.
The award marks the first time a bomber unit has been recognized with a President Unit Citation since the Vietnam War.
- Military Times, 10 hours ago: Under Hegseth, the OSS rides again — kind of.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth resurrected the OSS, created during the Second World War under "Wild Bill" Donovan.
- Military Times, 10 hours ago: VFW seeks veterans’ input on health care experiences in and out of VA.
Through early January, Veterans of Foreign Wars is conducting a survey of veterans on their health care experiences, including medical treatment received at the Department of Veterans Affairs or in private care.
The Caribbean - bottom line: ODPEM fiasco could scare off future donors, PNP warns.
- Jamaica Gleaner, just now: ODPEM fiasco could scare off future donors, PNP warns.
Local and international partners could become reluctant to donate to Jamaica in future national emergencies if confidence in the management of humanitarian aid is not urgently restored, Opposition Spokesperson on Local Government Natalie Neita Garvey has warned. This comes amid findings from a report by the auditor general that the Office of Disaster Preparedness and Emergency Management (ODPEM) misused funds donated for a Government-directed roof programme to clear third-party goods.
- Jamaica Gleaner, just now: Wright: They behave like hooligans but want to be called honourable.
WESTERN BUREAU: Amid deepening political rifts that have spilled from Gordon House into the courts, outspoken educator Linvern Wright is accusing some parliamentarians of abandoning principles, fairness and national responsibility in favour of partisan warfare.

South Asia - bottom line: Israeli strikes kill UNRWA worker, two others in Gaza.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 5 hours ago: Israeli strikes kill UNRWA worker, two others in Gaza.
CAIRO/JERUSALEM: Israeli airstrikes killed at least three people in Gaza on Monday, including a man working for the UN Palestinian refugee agency UNRWA, the relief age­ncy and local health officials said. The UNRWA worker, whom medics named as Adel Al-Helo, was working near a well in the Jabalia refugee camp in the enclave’s north, the agency and medics said. Three others were wounded in the strike, they said. “The initial reports indicate that the strike hit a target on the street near the water well, which was manned by UNRWA staff and a guard.
- Dawn (Pakistan), just now: Liberté, égalité, fatigué—the young are tired of everyone.
The writing was on the wall. Calls for mobilisation on 17 October had been followed by viral videos, parodying Japanese anime and Marvel productions to rally the troops. The streets had caught on: with each new day of mobilisation, walls became covered in angry, audacious graffiti, ranging from ‘F@ck the 17 (the generic number for the French police), bring on the 17th’ to ‘17 October, better than October 17 (the second of two revolutions in Russia in 1917)’. When the day finally arrived, a perfect storm swept across France, from its largest metropolitan areas to its mid-sized towns.

In Hinjewadi, Pune, a software engineer was arrested after allegedly killing his girlfriend during an argument. The couple had been in a relationship for three-and-a-half years and often fought over trivial issues. Following a dinner outing, a violent argument escalated, leading to the woman's death. Her cousin reported her unresponsiveness to the police, prompting their intervention. The police discovered her unconscious, and she was pronounced dead shortly after.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 14 hours ago: Manitoba couple get C$10,100 over neighbour's dogs; neighbour also wins C$1,000.
A Manitoba couple was awarded C$10,100 in damages due to ongoing issues with their neighbor's rescue dogs. Their neighbor's failure to control the animals led to numerous conflicts and trespassing incidents. The neighbor received C$1,000 for a separate incident involving broken dock boards. While both parties were found to have trespassed, the judge emphasized the difference in the nature of their actions.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: Nuclear weapon in space? Russia may launch warhead-capable satellite by December.
Russia is reportedly preparing to launch a satellite designed to carry a nuclear warhead by December. German intelligence has indicated that the satellite, known as Sputnik-S, has been assembled and stored for years. Dmitry Medvedev cites international law to justify potential nuclear weapon use, asserting state survival rights. He argues that international law permits nuclear usage in dire circumstances that threaten national existence.
